selectionReason: RC70 left a frozen NRCB2 run as the exact next experiment. It could distinguish cross-detector transport from a detector-specific calibration-support failure using already prepared public CAL data, a fixed DOLPHOT binary, and independently parseable diagnostics without opening any artificial-star or Cepheid outcome.
newVerifiedFacts: The NRCB2 parameter and DOLPHOT binary hashes matched the RC70 preregistration, and no prior NRCB2 output was overwritten.
The WCS-declared images 2, 6, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, and 30 alone produced positive alignment solutions; the other twenty-four images returned zero matches.
Supported NRCB2 images matched 1,339 to 1,535 stars with alignment sigma 0.08 to 0.15 pixel, passing the documented alignment guidance.
The NRCB2 run identified 98 global PSF stars and used only 91 to 96 per supported image, below the preregistered desirable count of 100.
Maximum absolute central-pixel PSF adjustment was 0.005902, below the documented 0.05 diagnostic threshold.
Supported images used 129 to 200 aperture stars, all above the documented desirable count of 100.
All seventy-two warning lines were the three expected structural diagnostics for each unsupported image; supported-image and unclassified warnings were zero.
The run wrote 29,382 catalogue rows in 44:59.74 with peak RSS 2,454,604 kB.
Node and independent Python parsers agreed exactly on all thirty-two alignment, PSF, and aperture rows, warning types, hashes, and gate decisions.
NRCB2 contained 2.078 times as many catalogue rows as NRCB1 and 356 to 496 more alignment matches, yet 25 to 29 fewer usable PSF stars per image.
The preregistered NRCB2 PSF gate failed; the two-detector, four-detector, artificial-star, distance, and Hubble-constant gates remain closed.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The NRCB1 measurement-operator qualification transfers unchanged to NRCB2.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: Every supported NRCB2 image passes alignment, PSF-star count, central adjustment, and aperture-star count.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Rejected under the preregistered gate because PSF-star counts were 91 to 96, although every other diagnostic passed.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: More detections and alignment matches guarantee adequate PSF calibration support.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: NRCB2 should have at least as many usable PSF stars as NRCB1 because its catalogue and alignment counts are larger.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Rejected for these frozen tiles: NRCB2 had 29,382 catalogue rows but fewer usable PSF stars than NRCB1.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: NRCB2 warnings indicate a failed reduction.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: Warnings occur in WCS-supported images or cannot be assigned to the preregistered detector topology.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Rejected: all seventy-two warnings were fully classified outside support, and supported images had zero warnings.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: Ninety-one to ninety-six PSF stars are sufficient for the required distance-scale accuracy despite missing the count proxy.
hypothesisAdjudication.prediction: A fresh spatial holdout and independent PSF-free flux check remain within a preregistered 0.01-mag residual boundary without threshold tuning.
hypothesisAdjudication.result: Open. The current PSF adjustment is small, but it was estimated from the calibration stars and is not an independent sufficiency test.

survivingHypotheses: NRCB2 may fail only a conservative calibration-support proxy while retaining adequate out-of-sample photometric accuracy.
Alternatively, crowding or spatial coverage may leave the PSF solution underconstrained in specific detector regions even though global detections are abundant.
A fresh validation, not post-hoc relaxation of the 100-star gate, is required to separate these explanations.
failedOrRejectedAttempts: Treating every zero-match image as an alignment failure is rejected by exact WCS support separation.
Using total catalogue rows as a proxy for PSF calibration support is rejected by the NRCB1/NRCB2 contrast.
Using alignment-star abundance as a proxy for PSF-star abundance is rejected by the same contrast.
Declaring success from the small central-pixel adjustment alone is disallowed because that statistic is not independent of the selected PSF stars.
Relaxing the 100-star rule after seeing 91 to 96 is disallowed; the original validation is preserved as a failed gate.

newCombination.name: Proxy-failure escalation to fresh PSF validation
newCombination.description: Instead of tuning the tile until a count threshold passes, preserve the failed count gate and test the quantity it proxies: spatially transported flux accuracy. Freeze a coordinate-hash validation split before residuals are read, compare NRCB1 and NRCB2 with the same withheld-star rule, and use an independent aperture or physics-based PSF prediction so the DOLPHOT calibration stars do not judge themselves.
newCombination.differenceFromPriorWork: DOLPHOT diagnostics, external PSF models, and held-out validation are established separately. RC71 proposes their explicit use as an escalation path after a preregistered proxy fails, while retaining the failed proxy and requiring fresh adjudication data. No novelty claim is made pending a broader literature review.

minimumDecisiveTest.input: Frozen NRCB1 and NRCB2 receipts, CAL hashes, WCS geometry, and a coordinate-hash rule specified before validation residuals are inspected.
minimumDecisiveTest.bottleneck: The 100-star gate fails, but its actual photometric consequence is unidentified.
minimumDecisiveTest.bridge: A PSF solution with fewer than 100 selected stars may be accepted only if it predicts flux for spatially withheld stars and an independent measurement agrees within a preregistered accuracy bound.
minimumDecisiveTest.adjudicand: Per-quadrant held-out PSF-minus-independent-aperture residual, spatial slope, tail residual, and first divergence from the NRCB1 control.
minimumDecisiveTest.success: Every preregistered spatial cell has adequate support and median cross-method residual at or below 0.01 mag, with no detector-specific tail or trend exceeding its frozen bound.
minimumDecisiveTest.rejection: An unsupported cell, residual above 0.01 mag, systematic spatial trend, parser disagreement, or any validation-driven change retires the candidate and requires a new holdout.
minimumDecisiveTest.stop: Do not run the sealed 3,072-row artificial-star experiment or infer Cepheid distances while the NRCB2 PSF-support question is unresolved.

uncertaintyBudget: Measurement error: independent aperture or physics-based PSF measurements have their own background and centering error and must be reported separately.
Model error: DOLPHOT and a comparison implementation may share upstream CAL and WCS systematics despite different flux estimators.
Sampling error: only 98 global PSF stars were reported, so spatial cells can be sparse even when the detector-wide count appears close to 100.
Selection error: choosing a larger tile, different PSF list, or relaxed threshold after viewing this result invalidates the current validation for the changed pipeline.
Transport error: NRCB1 and NRCB2 cover different sky and detector regions, so their contrast cannot yet be generalized to NRCB3, NRCB4, or the real Cepheid population.

connections.commonStructure: A proxy can pass at one stage while the target measurement remains unidentified: alignment abundance did not guarantee PSF support, just as nominal sample size does not guarantee target-population coverage and a clean selected run does not guarantee selective-error control.
connections.mapping: Catalogue rows and alignment matches map to available observations; usable PSF stars map to effective calibration support; fresh residual validation maps to out-of-sample risk; parameter changes map to adaptive selection events.
connections.validWhen: Support, proxy, target quantity, and adaptation history are recorded separately before the next validation outcome.
connections.breaksWhen: The count proxy is silently redefined, the failed run is deleted, or the same calibration stars and implementation are reused as final adjudicators.
connections.minimumTest: Require the same coordinate-hash holdout and independent flux comparison on NRCB1 and NRCB2 before accepting a proxy-failure rescue.

insufficientEvidence: Whether the 91 to 96 PSF stars yield biased flux outside the calibration sample.
Whether a larger common-support tile exists without weakening the frozen WCS margin.
Whether a curated external PSF-star list improves or biases spatial transport.
Whether NRCB3 and NRCB4 pass the original detector-level gate.
Any effect on artificial-star recovery, Cepheid photometry, component distance, or the Hubble constant.
safetyEthicsBoundary: The cycle uses public astronomical images and local computation. It performs no cyber-trust work, no human-subject inference, no autonomous telescope action, and no claim about cosmological resolution beyond the measured detector diagnostics.
claimBoundary: RC71 verifies a detector-specific PSF-star-count failure and exact independent reproduction. It does not prove that NRCB2 photometry is inaccurate, does not validate a rescue method, and does not estimate a Cepheid-distance or Hubble-constant effect.
exactNextStart: Before opening any new residual or artificial-star outcome, preregister a PSF-support rescue protocol. Preserve the failed NRCB2 tile as development data; define a coordinate-hash spatial holdout or a disjoint validation tile using WCS alone; select an independent aperture or physics-based PSF adjudicator; freeze per-cell support and a 0.01-mag residual boundary; then test the unchanged NRCB1 control and NRCB2 candidate. If the fresh validation fails, diagnose spatial support or calibration-star selection without relaxing the original receipt. If it passes, proceed to NRCB3 under the original gate while retaining NRCB2 as a separately justified exception rather than retroactively marking the 100-star gate as passed.
